QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_15

question.text: Additional/special margin in commodity futures is imposed when:

answer.text: Volatility increases significantly, or there's concentrated open interest not backed by warehouse stocks
A new member joins the exchange
The commodity price falls below MSP

explanation.text: The Logic: Indicators that trigger additional or special margin include a significant rise in volatility, concentrated open interest not backed by warehouse stocks (especially in agri commodities), and client-level concentration of open interest on the buy or sell side. Additional margin is levied on both sides; special margin is levied on one side only. The Trap: New membership, the MSP level, and elevated daily volume alone are not the triggers. The both-sides vs one-side distinction between additional and special margin is the structural detail to remember. Note: Before levying or revising additional/special margin, exchanges are expected to take the regulator's view rather than acting purely on their own assessment.
